title: The Tale of the Ox and the Donkey

paragraphs.en: In a prosperous countryside, a wealthy merchant lived with his family on a farm. He owned many camels and cattle and employed numerous workers. The merchant knew the language of all animals but kept it secret to avoid death.
paragraphs.zh: 在一个繁荣的乡村，一位富商和他的家人住在一座农场里。他拥有许多骆驼和牛，并雇用了众多工人。这位商人通晓所有动物的语言，但为了避祸，一直将这一秘密守口如瓶。

paragraphs.en: One day, as he sat beside his wife and watched his children play, he overheard an ox speaking to a donkey tied nearby. The ox said, "Watchful one, I hope you enjoy your comfort and service. Your ground is swept and watered, and they feed you sifted barley with clear, cool water.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，他坐在妻子身旁，看着孩子们玩耍时，无意间听到了一头牛在对 nearby 的驴子说话。牛说道：“警觉的你啊，希望你能享受舒适与服务。你的地面被打扫得干干净净并时常浇水，他们还给你喂食细筛过的麦芽，用的是清澈凉爽的水。”

paragraphs.en: In contrast, I am yoked at night, plowed under the whip all day until my sides are lacerated. They offer me beans mixed with mud and hay, and I spend nights in urine and dung. Meanwhile, you rest on well-tended ground."
paragraphs.zh: 相比之下，我晚上被套上轭，白天则在鞭子下犁地，直到皮肉鲜血淋漓。他们给我吃掺着泥巴和干草的豆子，夜晚还要在尿液和粪便中度过。而你却能在精心照料的土地上安眠。

paragraphs.en: The ox continued, "You stand in comfort, except when our master rides you briefly. You sleep while I toil endlessly."
paragraphs.zh: 公牛继续说道：“你倒挺自在，只是在主人偶尔骑你的时候除外。而我却不知疲倦地劳作。”

paragraphs.en: The donkey turned to the ox after he finished speaking. "Greenhorn," he said, "they were right to call you an ox because of your sincerity. You work hard for others without deceit.
paragraphs.zh: 公驴说完话后转向了牛，“生手，”他说，“他们把你叫做牛确实没错，因为你的确诚恳。你总是辛勤劳作，从不欺骗他人。”

paragraphs.en: Remember the saying 'Out of bad luck, they hastened on the road.' You labor from dawn till dusk at the plow until exhausted, only to be tied to the trough and beaten when you beg for food."
paragraphs.zh: 记得那句谚语：“祸不单行，反而催人上路。”你从黎明到黄昏在犁地，累得精疲力尽，结果却只能被拴在食槽前挨打，求乞食物。

paragraphs.en: The ox listened intently, convinced that the donkey's advice was sound. He thanked him and invoked God’s blessing, saying, "May you stay safe from harm, watchful one." The next day, the plowman brought the ox back to work.
paragraphs.zh: 公牛全神贯注地听着，深信驴子的建议是明智的。他向驴子道谢，并祈求上帝保佑：“愿你平安无恙，警醒之人。”第二天一早，犁夫便把公牛带回田里干活了。

paragraphs.en: Following the donkey’s counsel, the ox feigned weakness, falling on his belly when hit. This continued until nightfall.
paragraphs.zh: 遵照驴子的建议，牛装出虚弱的样子，一受击便趴倒在地。这一招直到夜幕降临才停止使用。

paragraphs.en: When the plowman returned home and tied the ox to the trough, he found him silent and withdrawn. Astonished, the plowman offered beans and fodder but received only a sniff and a retreat to the hay and straw. The next morning, the plowman discovered the trough untouched and the ox lying on his back, barely breathing.
paragraphs.zh: 当犁夫回到家，把牛拴在食槽旁时，发现牛沉默寡言，神情恍惚。犁夫惊讶之余，给牛喂了些豆子和饲料，却只换来一声鼻息和一头扎进干草堆里。第二天一早，犁夫发现食槽依旧空着，而牛仰面朝天，几乎停止了呼吸。

paragraphs.en: Feeling sorry for the ox, the plowman went to the merchant. "Master," he said, "last night, the ox refused to eat or touch his fodder."
paragraphs.zh: 农夫怜悯耕牛，便去找商人。“先生，”他说，“昨晚耕牛连饲料都不肯碰，也不吃了。”

paragraphs.en: The plowman followed the merchant's instructions and worked the donkey harshly until it finished the ox’s task. The exhausted donkey returned home at night, while the ox rested comfortably. Upon seeing the donkey, the ox praised its efforts and thanked God.
paragraphs.zh: 犁夫按照商人的吩咐，对驴子严加鞭策，直到它完成了牛的任务。疲惫不堪的驴子夜幕降临时才回家，而牛则舒适地休息着。见到驴子归来，牛称赞了它的努力，并向上帝表示感谢。

paragraphs.en: Seething with anger, the donkey thought, "This happened because of my curiosity. I must find a way to return the ox to his original state." He lay down in his trough, while the ox continued to rest and bless him.
paragraphs.zh: 气愤不已的驴子心想：“这一切都是因为我的好奇心。我必须找到办法让牛恢复原状。”它躺在槽子里，而牛则继续休息，并对着它祝福。

paragraphs.en: The donkey's daughter decided she would go to the king, despite her father’s warnings. She insisted on going, saying, "Father, I must do this." Her father warned her not to expose herself to danger but ultimately relented when she refused to change her mind.
paragraphs.zh: 驴子的女儿决定不顾父亲的警告，去见国王。她坚持要去，并说道：“爹爹，我必须这么做。”父亲劝阻她不要冒险，但最终拗不过她的固执。
